office.name: ODOT Commerce and Compliance Division - Over-Dimension Permit Unit (ORION)

fees.note: State of Oregon single-trip permit fee $8 (ORS 818.270 caps it at $8); one permit covers size and weight. County/City of Portland roads may add their own fee.

Road Use Assessment Fee for non-divisible loads over 98,000 lb, replaces weight-mile tax for the loaded trip. Cents per mile from ODOT table 9926 by gross weight AND axle count (e.g. 98,001-100,000 lb: 84c/mi on 5 axles, 15c/mi on 9 axles); over 240,000 lb computed by ODOT. Statutory basis 10.9c per ESAL-mile (ORS 818.225).

restrictions.text: Night travel (1/2 hr after sunset to 1/2 hr before sunrise): 8'7"-10' allowed on Interstates and Route Map 2 green routes only; 10'1"-12' Interstates only; over 12' not allowed at night anywhere.

Urban areas (Portland, Salem, Eugene, Grants Pass, Medford): over 12' wide no movement 7-9 AM and 4-6 PM on business days on non-Interstates, I-5 WA line-OR217 and I-5 exits 24-33; over 14' wide also barred on all Interstates in those hours and 11 AM-1 PM on all highways in those urban areas.

Summer weekends (last Monday in May to first Monday in September): after noon Saturday and all Sunday, up to 14' allowed on Interstates and authorized routes east of the Cascades, not on non-Interstates west of the Cascades; over 14' not allowed.

Holidays (New Year's, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas): no overwidth movement from noon the day before; up to 14' may resume on authorized routes per Attachment H schedule; over 14' not allowed through the holiday period.

notes: Pilot car counts differ by Route Map 2 color (green/purple/red) and Group Map 1 group; this file uses Interstate and green-route values. Single-trip permit special conditions take precedence.

Over 12' wide: certified flaggers (or the 3-pilot Certified Rolling Stop) required at listed tunnels/bridges (US26 Sunset Tunnel, several US101 bridges/tunnels, OR38, OR47, OR58, OR99E, OR126, OR138, OR238).
Superloads may need a Traffic Control Plan with certified flaggers and ODOT-monitored moves; ODOT bills monitoring/utility costs directly. Superload permits can take up to 10 days.
Overweight single-trip permits require a temporary pass or Oregon weight-mile tax account; weight-mile tax for 80,001-98,000 lb is a tax, not a permit fee, and is not modeled.
ORS 818.225 (RUAF) is amended by Enrolled HB 3991 (2025 special session), which was subject to possible referendum; check current RUAF rate table before relying on it.
Annual Non-Divisible permits and county/City of Portland routes out of scope.
